section_summary: This section continues a detailed survey of Japanese diplomatic and consular records in Argentina, including economic files, personnel rosters, and records destroyed or entrusted to Switzerland. It then documents Allied seizures, inventories, custody disputes, financial arrangements, leases, and proposed liquidation of Japanese mission property in Baghdad, Beirut, Bogotá, Mexico City, Prague, Vatican City, Egypt, Lisbon, and Santiago. The papers reveal differing views among Allied and protecting powers over access to archives, preservation or sale of property, treatment of funds, and repatriation of former Japanese personnel.

subfiles.title: Continuation of survey of Japanese Embassy and Consulate records in Argentina, folders 34-42
subfiles.about: This continuation inventories Japanese mission files in Argentina and records the disposition of mission documents at the rupture of relations.
subfiles.summary: The listed folders contain Argentine trade, finance, agriculture, industry, population, and economic reports from 1941-43, together with detailed rosters of locally employed embassy and consular staff. The survey also covers official vehicles, leased offices and residences, and reports on Argentine trade agreements and economic policy. Its final portion summarizes Ambassador Tomii's report that secret telegrams and documents were burned, while selected ordinary records and more than a thousand volumes were boxed or placed in a steel cabinet for Swiss custody.

subfiles.title: Contents of Trunk No. III entrusted by the former Japanese Embassy to the Swiss Legation
subfiles.about: The enclosure describes consular records found in a sealed Japanese trunk examined by Allied authorities.
subfiles.summary: Trunk III held registration and passport folders C-1 to C-20 and six ledgers from 1934, plus a February 1944 report on Argentina's Japanese community; the examiner judged detailed study useful for investigating Japanese residents.

subfiles.title: List of contents of index-card cabinets 18-26
subfiles.about: The enclosure describes registration and passport indexes for Japanese nationals in Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Index-card cabinets 18-26 held live and dead registration cards with biographical, passport and travel details and consular annotations; one traced a clandestine route from Brazil into Misiones Province.

subfiles.title: Telegram 487 on transfer of Japanese property in Baghdad
subfiles.about: The telegram reports the Allied takeover of Japanese diplomatic and consular property in Baghdad and requests disposal instructions.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 487: the Swedish chargé transferred Japanese property in Baghdad to U.S., British, Chinese and Soviet representatives; mostly furnishings, three locked steel cabinets may hold papers, and local archives seem thoroughly destroyed.

subfiles.title: Despatch 988 transmitting the Baghdad property inventory
subfiles.from: James S. Moose Jr., U.S. Legation, Baghdad
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards the inventory of Japanese diplomatic and consular property taken over in Baghdad.
subfiles.summary: Moose submits the Japanese property inventory continuing telegram 487 of December 12.

subfiles.title: Inventory of property left in the Imperial Japanese Legation at Baghdad
subfiles.about: This enclosure inventories the furniture, equipment, household goods, and books remaining in the Japanese Legation at Baghdad.
subfiles.summary: The inventory enumerates tables, flags, seals, safes, cabinets, chairs, carpets, lamps, tableware, Japanese porcelain, appliances, bedding, recreational equipment, films, and other effects. It notes that an air-conditioning apparatus belonged to a commercial firm and had been taken over by Baghdad's Controller of Foreign Property. The final pages list English, French, Arabic, German, and Japanese books on Asia, the Middle East, law, history, language, and diplomacy.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Beirut concerning French access to Japanese records
subfiles.about: The Department states that France was not among the powers designated to receive Japanese records but should be kept informed in Beirut.
subfiles.summary: Reply to the French aide-memoire excludes France from formal custody of Japanese records, but the Beirut legation should informally consult and keep the French delegate general advised.

subfiles.title: London telegram 10748 on German property in Syria and Lebanon
subfiles.about: The telegram relays British views on continued French sequestration of German property in Syria and Lebanon.
subfiles.summary: London telegram 10748: Britain's Economic Warfare Ministry and Foreign Office favor leaving German property under the French alien-property custodian, and think the Soviets not directly concerned under the Potsdam communique; repeated to Beirut, Paris and Moscow.

subfiles.title: Wadsworth memorandum on Japanese and German consular property in Beirut
subfiles.about: Wadsworth proposes additions to the Department's reply on Japanese archives and German property in Beirut.
subfiles.summary: Wadsworth recommends noting the French delegation in Beirut was informed as a courtesy, asking France about German archives and property in its sequestration and joint Allied custody, noting French administration of Italian property, and requesting instructions.

subfiles.title: Proposed note to the French chargé on Japanese records
subfiles.about: The proposed note explains the four-power basis for Allied custody of Japanese diplomatic and consular records.
subfiles.summary: Proposed note to the French chargé: Beirut action followed instructions based on decisions of the principal victorious powers, the U.S., Britain, the Soviet Union and China, acting together on Japanese records worldwide.

subfiles.title: Unsent telegram form to the American Legation at Beirut
subfiles.about: The telegram repeats instructions to exclude France from custody while consulting it informally in Syria and Lebanon.
subfiles.summary: Unsent telegram form to Beirut: France isn't authorized to receive Japanese records and property, but the legation should consult the French delegate general informally; marked not sent.

subfiles.title: Draft reply to the French Embassy's aide-mémoire
subfiles.about: The draft defends four-power control of Japanese archives while leaving the wider property question unresolved.
subfiles.summary: Draft reply to the French aide-memoire compares the Allied Japanese-archive decision with control of German archives abroad, argues against changing one while keeping the other, and notes French interests will be considered on property.

subfiles.title: Copy of note to the French chargé on Japanese archives
subfiles.about: The note states that four victorious powers were taking custody of Japanese diplomatic records and property worldwide.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the note to the French chargé: Beirut action conformed to a decision of the principal victorious powers, the U.S., Britain, the Soviet Union and China.

subfiles.title: Bogotá telegram 1477 on Swiss protection of Japanese nationals
subfiles.from: John C. Wiley, U.S. Embassy, Bogotá
subfiles.about: Wiley reports Swiss doubts about continuing to protect Japanese nationals without retaining access to the archives.
subfiles.summary: Bogota telegram 1477: the Swiss chargé says protecting Japanese nationals may be impracticable without the archives and sees no basis for treating German and Japanese nationals differently.

subfiles.title: Department reply on control and use of Japanese archives in Bogotá
subfiles.about: The Department permits Swiss use of necessary Japanese records while reserving strict Allied control of the archives.
subfiles.summary: State replies Swiss representatives should have full access to records needed to protect Japanese interests, while custody stays under the American, British, Soviet and Chinese missions; avoid a procedural distinction from German cases.

subfiles.title: Handwritten forwarding note
subfiles.about: The note forwards a further report in connection with a despatch mentioned the previous day.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten forwarding note saying a further report is sent in connection with an earlier despatch.

subfiles.title: Despatch 27,744 on Japanese archives and property in Mexico
subfiles.from: George S. Messersmith, U.S. Embassy, Mexico City
subfiles.about: Messersmith forwards Sweden's answers about Japanese archives, assets, property, accounts, and leases in Mexico.
subfiles.summary: Messersmith's Despatch 27,744 encloses the Swedish minister's reply, the July 9 Portugal-to-Sweden transfer protocol, a property inventory and the former chancery lease, calling the data self-explanatory.

subfiles.title: Swedish minister's report on Japanese interests in Mexico
subfiles.about: The Swedish minister itemizes the Japanese archives, assets, expenses, and leased chancery under his care in Mexico.
subfiles.summary: Swedish minister De Ribbing lists twelve files on Japanese residents, firms and correspondence, no immovable property, movable property and liquid assets, and the reduced peso fund; monthly payments cover residents, the chancery lease, a guardian, a gardener and utilities.

subfiles.title: Protocol transferring Japanese interests in Mexico from Portugal to Sweden
subfiles.about: The protocol transfers Japanese funds, archives, furniture, and contracts in Mexico from Portuguese to Swedish custody.
subfiles.summary: Protocol: Portugal's minister hands Sweden's minister peso and dollar cheques, frozen accounts, a bankbook, twelve archive files, Japanese Legation and attache furniture, the chancery lease and electricity contract.

subfiles.title: Inventory of Japanese Legation furniture and utensils in Mexico
subfiles.about: The inventory lists 844 pieces associated with the former Japanese Legation and its attachés in Mexico City.
subfiles.summary: The document separates property at the former chancery, effects moved from Minister Yoshiaki Miura's residence, and property belonging to the military and naval attachés. Items include filing cabinets, desks, safes, furniture, beds, radios, typewriters, appliances, books, artwork, and dining utensils. The stated total is 844 pieces.

subfiles.title: Furniture ceded to the Japanese Mutual Aid Committee in Mexico
subfiles.about: The list identifies former Japanese Legation furniture transferred to the Japanese Mutual Aid Committee with Japanese Government authorization.
subfiles.summary: List of ninety-seven furniture and office pieces ceded to the Japanese Mutual Aid Committee in Mexico, deducted from the inventory transferred to Sweden.

subfiles.title: Lease of the former Japanese Legation chancery at Orizaba 36
subfiles.from: José dos Santos Silva Taveira and the Tazzer co-owners
subfiles.about: The contract continues the lease of Orizaba 36 for use in representing Japanese interests in Mexico.
subfiles.summary: The Portuguese chargé, acting for Japanese interests, agrees with the Tazzer owners to continue the former Japanese Legation lease. Rent rises to 975 pesos from March 1943, with advance monthly payments and an initial two-year binding term. The contract regulates notice, use, subletting, alterations, repairs, and liability for damage.

subfiles.title: Prague telegram 761 on absence of Japanese government property
subfiles.from: Laurence A. Steinhardt, U.S. Embassy, Prague
subfiles.about: The telegram reports that no Japanese archives or other government property could be found in Czechoslovakia.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office reported that a minute search found no Japanese government archives or property. It stated that Japan had presented its former Prague legation building to Germany in 1942. The building was taken over in 1945 as German state property for use by the Czechoslovak state.

subfiles.title: Telegram to SCAP concerning the Japanese ambassador at Vatican City
subfiles.to: Dean Acheson, Acting Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Department asks Tokyo to address the absence of instructions to the Japanese ambassador at the Vatican.
subfiles.summary: Telegram to SCAP: Japan's Vatican ambassador still lacks directions on records and property; the Holy See sees the Allied directive as suspending, not rupturing, relations since it isn't causing the interruption.

subfiles.title: Routing notation on restricted distribution
subfiles.about: The notation records that an attached item was withheld from several U.S. agencies.
subfiles.summary: Note that the attachment was withheld from War, Navy, OSS and FBI distribution on December 20, 1945.

subfiles.title: Bogotá telegram 1499 requesting a Japanese-language archives examiner
subfiles.from: John C. Wiley, U.S. Embassy, Bogotá
subfiles.about: Wiley reports the imminent takeover of voluminous Japanese archives and requests a qualified language specialist.
subfiles.summary: Bogota telegram 1499: the Soviet minister offered to send an archives examiner; Wiley suggests State send its own Japanese-language examiner promptly, noting the records' volume and the former Japanese minister's indiscretion.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Dublin on Japanese compliance with Allied instructions
subfiles.about: The Department relays Tokyo's report that the Japanese consul general in Dublin was ordered to comply immediately.
subfiles.summary: Telegram to Dublin: a delayed December 19 Tokyo message says Japan is directing its consul general to stop disputing and comply immediately with Allied instructions.

subfiles.title: Vatican City telegram 240 on suspension of Japanese relations
subfiles.from: Franklin C. Gowen, U.S. Mission, Vatican City
subfiles.about: Gowen reports Harada's lack of instructions and the Holy See's view that relations with Japan would merely be suspended.
subfiles.summary: Vatican telegram 240: Harada said he had no order from Tokyo to sever relations and awaits instructions; Gowen urges Japan to issue directions promptly; the Holy See stresses the interruption is suspension, not rupture.

subfiles.title: Vatican City telegram 241 concerning keys to Japanese archives in Italy
subfiles.from: Franklin C. Gowen, U.S. Mission, Vatican City
subfiles.about: The telegram seeks instructions compelling Harada to surrender keys to the former Japanese Embassy archives in Italy.
subfiles.summary: Vatican telegram 241: Ambassador Kirk wants the keys to Japanese archives in Italy without forcing rooms under Allied control; Sweden doesn't object, but Harada has the keys and refuses to surrender them without Japan's instructions.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram 215 ordering Japanese compliance in Dublin
subfiles.about: Acheson reports that Japan was ordering its consul general to comply with Allied instructions.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo telegram 215: Japan is directing its Dublin consul general to stop quibbling and comply immediately; transmission was delayed by non-receipt of the original.

subfiles.title: Blank Office Memorandum form
subfiles.about: The page is an otherwise blank United States Government Office Memorandum form.
subfiles.summary: No substantive memorandum text, sender, recipient, or subject is present. Only the printed form and an indistinct date marking appear.

subfiles.title: Egyptian note requesting custody of Japanese archives and property
subfiles.about: Egypt requests American agreement that it retain Japanese mission archives and property while allowing four-power access.
subfiles.summary: Egypt, as a belligerent ally, claims the right to preserve Japanese archives and property, offers the four powers access, and cites its custody of German mission property; Switzerland doesn't object if the representatives agree.

subfiles.title: Despatch 615 transmitting report on Japanese records and property in Portugal
subfiles.from: Herman B. Baruch, U.S. Embassy, Lisbon
subfiles.about: Baruch forwards a detailed report on Allied administration of Japanese records and property in Portugal.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 615: American, British and Chinese missions have held Japanese property in Portugal jointly since November 13; the enclosed report ends with nine recommendations or requests for instructions; copies to Madrid and London.

subfiles.title: Custody of Official Japanese Property and Records in Portugal
subfiles.to: U.S. Embassy, Lisbon and Department of State
subfiles.about: The memorandum details the takeover, administration, and proposed disposition of Japanese government records, funds, premises, property, and personnel in Portugal.
subfiles.summary: American, British, and Chinese representatives took custody on November 13, sealing premises and examining records after the Japanese mission closed. The surviving archives were routine because confidential material had been destroyed; the committee also inventoried more than 26 million escudos, bank accounts, leases, vehicles, furnishings, films, books, and personal baggage. It discussed advances to the Siamese Legation, storage and sale of property, repatriation of forty-seven Japanese personnel, and the status of offices in Timor and Macau. Nine recommendations sought authority concerning archives, leases, public sale, private effects, claims, the former consul at Perpignan, telegram costs, and Yokohama Specie Bank funds.

subfiles.title: Telegram to SCAP reporting Vatican representative's readiness to comply
subfiles.to: Dean Acheson, Acting Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Department reports that the Japanese representative at Vatican City was prepared to carry out newly received instructions.
subfiles.summary: Telegram to SCAP: the Japanese representative told the Holy See he is ready to implement the instructions he has now received.

subfiles.title: Vatican City telegram 243 on application of the October 5 directive
subfiles.from: Franklin C. Gowen, U.S. Mission, Vatican City
subfiles.about: Gowen reports that Harada had learned the Japanese Government's October 5 directive applied to the Vatican.
subfiles.summary: Vatican telegram 243: Montini told Gowen that Harada received a Japanese communication confirming the October 5 directive covers the Vatican mission; more detailed instructions are expected.

subfiles.title: Department instruction answering Lisbon's nine recommendations
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Lisbon
subfiles.about: The Department approves the Lisbon committee's work and answers its questions about Japanese archives, property, expenses, and funds.
subfiles.summary: State answers Lisbon's nine recommendations: no archive destruction, send the Siamese receipts, early lease vacation approved, store property but sell official property if storage is impracticable, claims deferred to a Reparations Commission, custodial expenses payable from Japanese funds, no special treatment for Yokohama Specie Bank funds.

subfiles.title: Despatch 13,246 on disposal of Japanese archives and property in Chile
subfiles.from: Claude G. Bowers, U.S. Embassy, Santiago
subfiles.about: Bowers requests expedited instructions for disposing of Japanese archives and movable property taken over in Chile.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 13,246: after the November transfer to Bowers, British instructions favor sending archives to Washington with British access, selling movable property and a joint proceeds account; Bowers recommends getting Soviet and Chinese approval and authorizing the sale.
